source: sanitized Windows vendor-API output-state flag negative hardware-effect probe

live_validation.procedure: with Lewitt Control Center closed, choose an output pair above -60 dB with zero state flags; set only its paired state flags for five seconds; read back; restore the exact original 40-byte block; read back
live_validation.api_result: both temporary state flags read back as 1 and the exact original 40-byte block was restored and matched
live_validation.physical_output_result: later user verification established that changing these flags does not mute the physical output
live_validation.result: byte write, read-back, and exact restoration passed, but the physical mute hypothesis failed
live_validation.production_path_test: removed after the physical mute hypothesis was disproved

limitations: Recovered vendor code writes these flags when the paired hardware gain equals -60 dB; output-gain writes keep them synchronized only as endpoint fields.
These bytes are not an independent hardware mute and must not be exposed as OutputMute.
The official control center's visible DSP mute uses host-filter property 400 instead.
The underlying USB setup packet has not been captured with USBPcap.
